segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have another holiday lesson for you guys.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们为你们准备了另一个假期课程。

segments.en: It's an intermediate level lesson, but it's not about Christmas and it's not about New Year's.
segments.zh: 这是一个中级课程，但它不是关于圣诞节，也不是关于新年的。

segments.en: So what's this holiday, Marco?
segments.zh: 那么这个假期是什么，马可？

segments.en: It's like after Christmas, but before New Year's.
segments.zh: 就像圣诞节之后，但在新年之前。

segments.en: Okay, so let's look at this holiday in today's vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 好的，让我们在今天的词汇预览中看看这个假期。

segments.en: Vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预习。

segments.en: All right, so as you noticed in the title, this is called Boxing Day.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如您在标题中注意到的那样，这称为节礼日。

segments.en: So like fighting boxing or...
segments.zh: 所以喜欢打拳击或...

segments.en: No, no, no.
segments.zh: 不，不，不。

segments.en: Kind of like boxes, right?
segments.zh: 有点像盒子，对吧？

segments.en: It's more related to boxes.
segments.zh: 它与盒子有关。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So this is a holiday that we don't actually celebrate in America.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个我们实际上并没有在美国庆祝的节日。

segments.en: It's celebrated in what are called Commonwealth countries.
segments.zh: 它在所谓的英联邦国家庆祝。

segments.en: That means countries that used to be a part of Great Britain or that are a part of Great Britain.
segments.zh: 这意味着曾经是英国的一部分或是英国的一部分的国家。

segments.en: So England, Scotland, Canada, Australia.
segments.zh: 所以英格兰，苏格兰，加拿大，澳大利亚。

segments.en: And this is a day where, well, it's considered a holiday because it's a bank holiday.
segments.zh: 这是一个假期，因为它是银行假期，所以它被认为是假期。

segments.en: That means all the banks close.
segments.zh: 这意味着所有银行都关闭。

segments.en: No one's at work.
segments.zh: 没有人在工作。

segments.en: It's the day after Christmas.
segments.zh: 这是圣诞节后的第二天。

segments.en: So it's December 26th and it's traditionally a day when you give money or gifts to the poor.
segments.zh: 所以现在是 12 月 26 日，传统上是你给穷人钱或礼物的日子。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And so this is more or less what we're going to be talking about, but more modern, right?
segments.zh: 所以这或多或少是我们将要谈论的，但更现代，对吧？

segments.en: Before it was like that, but now it's kind of become this shopping thing, right?
segments.zh: 以前是这样的，但现在它有点成为这种购物的东西，对吧？

segments.en: It has.
segments.zh: 它有。

segments.en: It's a day when everyone goes to the sales after Christmas to return things or to buy new things.
segments.zh: 这是圣诞节后每个人都去销售退货或购买新东西的一天。

segments.en: So we're going to hear about this right away in today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以我们将在今天的对话中立即听到这一点。

segments.en: And when we come back, we'll be talking about some of the phrases and words that you've heard.
segments.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将谈论您听到的一些短语和单词。

segments.en: What do you think of this one?
segments.zh: 你怎么看这一款？

segments.en: Eh, so-so.
segments.zh: 嗯，一般般。

segments.en: And this one?
segments.zh: 那这件呢？

segments.en: Too flashy?
segments.zh: 太花哨了吗？

segments.en: Nah, not too flashy.
segments.zh: 没有，不太花哨。

segments.en: Oh, and this sweater from my aunt.
segments.zh: 哦，还有我姑姑的这件毛衣。

segments.en: Isn't it hideous?
segments.zh: 是不是很丑？

segments.en: I guess.
segments.zh: 我想是吧。

segments.en: Are you even listening?
segments.zh: 你到底有没有在听？

segments.en: I'm trying to have a conversation with you.
segments.zh: 我想和你谈谈。

segments.en: And I'm trying to watch the game, but you're yapping on about your new clothes.
segments.zh: 可我正想看比赛，你却一直念叨你的新衣服。

segments.en: Well I have to decide which gifts to keep and which to exchange for better ones when I go to the Boxing Day sales this afternoon.
segments.zh: 我下午要去逛节礼日促销，得先决定留下哪些礼物，哪些拿去换成更好的。

segments.en: Well could you do me the favor of making this quick?
segments.zh: 好吧，你能帮我快点做这个吗？

segments.en: It's the third quarter and you've been blabbering on since the first.
segments.zh: 都第三节了，你从第一节开始就一直说个没完。

segments.en: Oh, your precious game.
segments.zh: 哦，你那宝贝比赛。

segments.en: You watch the same game every year and each year your beloved hometown team loses by at least three goals.
segments.zh: 您每年观看相同的比赛，每年您心爱的家乡球队至少输掉三个进球。

segments.en: Oh, no you didn't.
segments.zh: 你居然敢这么说！

segments.en: You didn't just insult the Salisbury Seals, did you?
segments.zh: 你不只是侮辱了索尔兹伯里海豹队，是吗？

segments.en: Why don't you just go return all those stupid clothes and not come back until the sales are over?
segments.zh: 你干脆把那些破衣服全退了，等促销结束再回来吧。

segments.en: I might just.
segments.zh: 我可能还真会。

segments.en: Enjoy your stupid game.
segments.zh: 好好看你的破比赛吧。

segments.en: And Merry Christmas.
segments.zh: 还有，圣诞快乐。

segments.en: Merry Christmas.
segments.zh: 圣诞快乐。

segments.en: Alright, great, so we're back and interesting, the couple fighting right after Christmas.
segments.zh: 好吧，太好了，所以我们回来了，很有趣，这对夫妇在圣诞节后打架。

segments.en: Well I think it's very common to hear fights around the holidays.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为在假期周围听到打架是很常见的。

segments.en: People are very stressed out.
segments.zh: 人们压力很大。

segments.en: And tired of dealing with family and presents and all the stress, right?
segments.zh: 厌倦了与家人和礼物以及所有的压力打交道，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: But we'll talk about that a little bit later on.
segments.zh: 但我们稍后会讨论这个问题。

segments.en: Right now why don't we take a look at four key words in language takeaway.
segments.zh: 现在我们为什么不看看语言外卖中的四个关键词。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Okay, these first two words are words that the wife uses in talking about some of these clothes that she got as presents.
segments.zh: 好吧，这前两个词是妻子在谈论她作为礼物得到的一些衣服时使用的词。

segments.en: So she says, well she asks her husband, is this too flashy?
segments.zh: 所以她说，好吧，她问她的丈夫，这太浮华了吗？

segments.en: Flashy.
segments.zh: 华丽。

segments.en: Alright, so you know flash, like the camera flash, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你知道闪光灯，就像相机闪光灯，对吧？

segments.en: This big light.
segments.zh: 这个大灯。

segments.en: Now flashy when you're talking about clothes or an object, it's too noticeable, right?
segments.zh: 现在当你谈论衣服或物体时，它太明显了，对吧？

segments.en: It's too noticeable, too bright, too loud.
segments.zh: 它太明显，太亮，太响亮。

segments.en: So for example, a black shirt is not flashy.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，黑色衬衫并不浮华。

segments.en: But an orange shirt.
segments.zh: 而是一件橙色的衬衫。

segments.en: An orange shirt with buttons and bells and rhinestones, diamonds, that's flashy.
segments.zh: 一件带有纽扣和铃铛和水钻、钻石的橙色衬衫，这很华丽。

segments.en: She can also mean something that is supposed to look expensive.
segments.zh: 她也可以指一些应该看起来很昂贵的东西。

segments.en: Okay, so that sweater was a little bit flashy according to her.
segments.zh: 好吧，按照她的说法，那件毛衣有点浮华。

segments.en: But also she talked about another sweater being hideous.
segments.zh: 但她也谈到另一件毛衣丑陋。

segments.en: So hideous is an ugly word and it means ugly.
segments.zh: 如此丑陋是一个丑陋的词，它的意思是丑陋的。

segments.en: Ugly.
segments.zh: 丑陋。

segments.en: Okay, so I could say this sweater is hideous.
segments.zh: 好吧，我可以说这件毛衣很丑。

segments.en: That means it's not only ugly, it's really ugly.
segments.zh: 这意味着它不仅丑陋，而且真的很丑。

segments.en: Okay, it's more than ugly.
segments.zh: 好吧，它不仅仅是丑陋的。

segments.en: Alright, a hideous sweater.
segments.zh: 好吧，一件丑陋的毛衣。

segments.en: And moving on, the guy now was a little bit irritated and stressed out and he said, you keep yapping on about your new clothes.
segments.zh: 继续前进，这家伙现在有点恼火和压力过大，他说，你一直在为你的新衣服大喊大叫。

segments.en: So what is this yapping on?
segments.zh: 那么这个叫喊是什么？

segments.en: Well, yap is a sound like yap, yap, yap, yap, yap, yap, yap, yap.
segments.zh: 嗯，Yap 是一种声音，如 Yap、Yap、Yap、Yap、Yap、Yap、Yap、Yap。

segments.en: So yapping, to yap on about means to continue to talk and talk and talk about something.
segments.zh: 所以大喊大叫，喋喋不休意味着继续谈论、谈论和谈论某事。

segments.en: Because he's watching the football game on TV and she's talking and talking and talking and he's annoyed.
segments.zh: 因为他在电视上看足球比赛，她在说话、说话、说话，他很生气。

segments.en: So this is rude to say, stop yapping about this or stop yapping on about your game.
segments.zh: 所以这是不礼貌的，停止大喊大叫或停止对你的游戏大喊大叫。

segments.en: It's very rude.
segments.zh: 这很粗鲁。

segments.en: It means just stop talking.
segments.zh: 这意味着停止说话。

segments.en: I'm annoyed.
segments.zh: 我很生气。

segments.en: And well, then he mentioned another phrase that is pretty much the same thing, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，然后他提到了另一个几乎相同的短语，对吧？

segments.en: Blabbering on.
segments.zh: 喋喋不休。

segments.en: To blabber, to blabber on about means to talk about something but to not really make sense.
segments.zh: 喋喋不休，喋喋不休意味着谈论某事但没有真正意义。

segments.en: Okay, so it's just worthless talk.
segments.zh: 好吧，这只是一文不值的谈话。

segments.en: So you're just talking to talk.
segments.zh: 所以你只是在说话。

segments.en: You're not really saying anything interesting.
segments.zh: 你真的没有说什么有趣的话。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And so sometimes we make fun of people who blabber on about things because they're not important to us or they sound stupid.
segments.zh: 所以有时我们会取笑那些喋喋不休的人，因为他们对我们不重要，或者听起来很愚蠢。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Okay, so four key words there.
segments.zh: 好吧，有四个关键词。

segments.en: Blabbering on, yapping on.
segments.zh: 继续说下去，大喊大叫。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to them again in the dialogue?
segments.zh: 我们为什么不在对话中再听他们的？

segments.en: What do you think of this one?
segments.zh: 你怎么看这一款？

segments.en: Eh, so-so.
segments.zh: 嗯，一般般。

segments.en: And this one?
segments.zh: 那这件呢？

segments.en: Too flashy?
segments.zh: 太花哨了吗？

segments.en: Nah, not too flashy.
segments.zh: 没有，不太花哨。

segments.en: Oh, and this sweater from my aunt, isn't it hideous?
segments.zh: 哦，还有我姑姑的这件毛衣，是不是很可怕？

segments.en: I guess.
segments.zh: 我想是吧。

segments.en: Are you even listening?
segments.zh: 你到底有没有在听？

segments.en: I'm trying to have a conversation with you.
segments.zh: 我想和你谈谈。

segments.en: And I'm trying to watch the game, but you're yapping on about your new clothes.
segments.zh: 可我正想看比赛，你却一直念叨你的新衣服。

segments.en: Well, I have to decide which gifts to keep and which to exchange for better ones when I go to the Boxing Day sales this afternoon.
segments.zh: 好吧，当我今天下午去节礼日销售时，我必须决定保留哪些礼物以及换哪些更好的礼物。

segments.en: Well, could you do me the favor of making this quick?
segments.zh: 好吧，你能帮我快点做这个吗？

segments.en: It's the third quarter and you've been blabbering on since the first.
segments.zh: 都第三节了，你从第一节开始就一直说个没完。

segments.en: Oh, your precious game.
segments.zh: 哦，你那宝贝游戏。

segments.en: You watch the same game every year and each year your beloved hometown team loses by at least three goals.
segments.zh: 您每年观看相同的比赛，每年您心爱的家乡球队至少输掉三个进球。

segments.en: Oh, no you didn't.
segments.zh: 你居然敢这么说！

segments.en: You didn't just insult the Salisbury Seals, did you?
segments.zh: 你不只是侮辱了索尔兹伯里海豹队，是吗？

segments.en: Why don't you just go return all those stupid clothes and not come back until the sales are over?
segments.zh: 你干脆把那些破衣服全退了，等促销结束再回来吧。

segments.zh: 我可能还真会。

segments.zh: 还有，圣诞快乐。

segments.en: Merry Christmas.

segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay, so this first phrase is very closely related to the days after Christmas, especially here on Boxing Day.
segments.zh: 好的，所以这第一个短语与圣诞节后的日子非常密切相关，尤其是在节礼日。

segments.en: We've got someone who's talking about going to the stores, to the sales to exchange her gifts for better gifts.
segments.zh: 我们有人在谈论去商店，去销售她的礼物以换取更好的礼物。

segments.en: Okay, to exchange something for something better.
segments.zh: 好吧，用更好的东西换东西。

segments.en: This is a very common construction.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常常见的结构。

segments.en: It's an important phrase when talking about shopping.
segments.zh: 在谈论购物时，这是一个重要的短语。

segments.en: So when we look at this construction, you would say, to exchange this sweater for a better one or for a larger one.
segments.zh: 因此，当我们看到这种结构时，您会说，将这件毛衣换成一件更好的或更大的一件。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you can change the adjective, the word that's describing it.
segments.zh: 所以你可以改变形容词，描述它的词。

segments.en: So you can say, to exchange these shoes for bigger ones.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，把这些鞋换成更大的鞋子。

segments.en: I could also joke and I could say, I'm going to exchange my boyfriend for a better one if he's being rude to me.
segments.zh: 我也可以开玩笑，我可以说，如果他对我无礼，我会用我的男朋友换一个更好的。

segments.en: Okay, so to exchange something for something else.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以用一些东西换东西。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And then we saw another phrase that the husband replied to when she offended him with his football team.
segments.zh: 然后我们看到了丈夫在他的足球队冒犯他时回答的另一个短语。

segments.en: He said, oh no, you didn't.
segments.zh: 他说，哦不，你没有。

segments.en: Didn't what?
segments.zh: 没有什么？

segments.en: I know, didn't what?
segments.zh: 我知道，没有什么？

segments.en: No, you didn't what?
segments.zh: 不，你没有什么？

segments.en: All right, so this, like you said, doesn't make sense alone, but some cultural context might help.
segments.zh: 好吧，就像你说的那样，这并没有意义，但一些文化背景可能会有所帮助。

segments.en: In English, we often say this phrase to mean, oh no, you didn't just say that.
segments.zh: 在英语中，我们经常说这个短语的意思是，哦不，你不只是这么说。

segments.en: Oh, you didn't just insult my team.
segments.zh: 哦，你不只是侮辱我的团队。

segments.en: He's saying, I can't believe you just said that.
segments.zh: 他说，我不敢相信你只是这么说的。

segments.en: He's upset because what she said was rude or mean.
segments.zh: 他很沮丧，因为她说的是粗鲁或刻薄的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So I could say, you know, Marco, I think Ecuador sucks.
segments.zh: 所以我可以说，你知道，马可，我认为厄瓜多尔很糟糕。

segments.en: Oh, no, you didn't.
segments.zh: 哦，不，你没有。

segments.en: I did just say, I don't think so actually, but it's usually a response, right?
segments.zh: 我只是说，我实际上不这么认为，但这通常是一种回应，对吧？

segments.en: You have to wait until somebody maybe says something mean or something that, you know, really hurts her feelings or you don't agree with when you respond to this, but you're usually very, very offended, right?
segments.zh: 你必须等到有人说出什么刻薄的话，你知道，真的会伤害她的感情，或者你不同意你的反应，但你通常会非常非常被冒犯，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: It's always a response to a comment that has made you angry or upset.
segments.zh: 它总是对让你生气或不高兴的评论的回应。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And then our last phrase is when they finished talking and they were fighting, she left and said, I might just.
segments.zh: 然后我们的最后一句话是当他们说完他们正在打架时，她离开并说，我可能只是。

segments.en: Just what?
segments.zh: 只是什么？

segments.en: I know, just what?
segments.zh: 我知道，只是什么？

segments.en: See, again, these are common phrases, but they don't seem to make much sense alone.
segments.zh: 再说一遍，这些是常见的短语，但它们似乎没有多大意义。

segments.en: I might just.
segments.zh: 我可能还真会。

segments.en: So let's listen to, this is a response again.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听听，这又是一个回应。

segments.en: This is a response to the line before it.
segments.zh: 这是对它之前的线的响应。

segments.zh: 你为什么不只是去把所有那些愚蠢的衣服都归还，直到很久以后才回来？

segments.en: And she says, I might just, I might just do exactly what you just said.
segments.zh: 她说，我可能只是，我可能只是按照你刚才说的去做。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: She's threatening him.
segments.zh: 她在威胁他。

segments.en: She's saying, I might just go out and not come back for 10 hours.
segments.zh: 她说，我可能只是出去 10 小时不回来。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I might just do that.
segments.zh: 我可能会这样做。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's a way to say what you said.
segments.zh: 所以这是说你说的话的一种方式。

segments.en: I might do that.
segments.zh: 我可能会这样做。

segments.en: And I'm threatening you.
segments.zh: 我在威胁你。

segments.en: So again, it's usually a response, right?
segments.zh: 再说一次，它通常是一种回应，对吧？

segments.en: Or a threat, as you said.
segments.zh: 或威胁，正如你所说的。

segments.en: So I can say, Marco, why don't you just leave?
segments.zh: 所以我可以说，马可，你为什么不离开呢？

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I might just.
segments.zh: 我可能还真会。

segments.en: Oh, what am I going to do in the studio alone?
segments.zh: 哦，我一个人在工作室要做什么？

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So three interesting phrases there.
segments.zh: 所以那里有三个有趣的短语。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to all the words and phrases again in our dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不在上次的对话中再次听所有的单词和短语。

segments.en: What do you think of this one?
segments.zh: 你怎么看这一款？

segments.en: Eh, so-so.
segments.zh: 嗯，一般般。

segments.en: And this one?
segments.zh: 那这件呢？

segments.en: Too flashy?
segments.zh: 太花哨了吗？

segments.en: Nah, not too flashy.
segments.zh: 没有，不太花哨。

segments.en: Oh, and this sweater from my aunt, isn't it hideous?
segments.zh: 哦，还有我姑姑的这件毛衣，是不是很可怕？

segments.en: I guess.
segments.zh: 我想是吧。

segments.en: Are you even listening?
segments.zh: 你到底有没有在听？

segments.en: I'm trying to have a conversation with you.
segments.zh: 我想和你谈谈。

segments.en: And I'm trying to watch the game, but you're yapping on about your new clothes.
segments.zh: 可我正想看比赛，你却一直念叨你的新衣服。

segments.en: Well, I have to decide which gifts to keep and which to exchange for better ones when I go to the Boxing Day sales this afternoon.
segments.zh: 好吧，当我今天下午去节礼日销售时，我必须决定保留哪些礼物以及换哪些更好的礼物。

segments.en: Well, could you do me the favor of making this quick?
segments.zh: 好吧，你能帮我快点做这个吗？

segments.en: It's the third quarter and you've been blabbering on since the first.
segments.zh: 都第三节了，你从第一节开始就一直说个没完。

segments.en: Oh, your precious game.
segments.zh: 哦，你那宝贝游戏。

segments.en: You watch the same game every year and each year your beloved hometown team loses by at least three goals.
segments.zh: 您每年观看相同的比赛，每年您心爱的家乡球队至少输掉三个进球。

segments.en: Oh, no you didn't.
segments.zh: 你居然敢这么说！

segments.en: You didn't just insult the Salisbury Seals, did you?
segments.zh: 你不只是侮辱了索尔兹伯里海豹队，是吗？

segments.en: Why don't you just go return all those stupid clothes and not come back until the sales are over?
segments.zh: 你干脆把那些破衣服全退了，等促销结束再回来吧。

segments.en: I might just.
segments.zh: 我可能还真会。

segments.en: Enjoy your stupid game.
segments.zh: 好好玩你那破游戏吧。

segments.en: And Merry Christmas.
segments.zh: 还有，圣诞快乐。

segments.en: Merry Christmas.
segments.zh: 圣诞快乐。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So Boxing Day, as you said, is usually a Commonwealth thing.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，节礼日通常是联邦的事情。

segments.en: In the United States, you don't really have it, right?
segments.zh: 在美国，你真的没有，对吧？

segments.en: We do not.
segments.zh: 我们没有。

segments.en: My family, I don't know why, but my family sometimes celebrates that we have friends who come over and we have a nice Boxing Day meal.
segments.zh: 我的家人，我不知道为什么，但我的家人有时会庆祝我们有朋友过来，我们有一顿美味的节礼日餐。

segments.en: But I've been told that the tradition in Commonwealth countries is to watch sporting events, local sporting events, and to go shopping for all these sales and bargains and exchange all those ugly, hideous, annoying or bad gifts that you received at Christmas.
segments.zh: 但我被告知，英联邦国家的传统是观看体育赛事、当地体育赛事，并购买所有这些销售和便宜货，并交换所有您在圣诞节收到的丑陋、丑陋、烦人或糟糕的礼物。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's usually like the after Christmas sales.
segments.zh: 所以它通常就像圣诞节后的销售一样。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So if you have any special Boxing Day traditions, I'd be very curious to hear them.
segments.zh: 所以如果你有任何特殊的节礼日传统，我很想听听他们的意见。

segments.en: Again, not a holiday related to the sport boxing.
segments.zh: 同样，不是与体育拳击有关的假期。

segments.en: It's spelled the same way and it looks the same, but they're very different.
segments.zh: 它的拼写方式相同，看起来相同，但它们非常不同。

segments.en: So if you have any stories or questions about the things that we talked about today, please do let us know on our website EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您对我们今天讨论的内容有任何故事或问题，请在我们的网站 englishpod.com 上告诉我们。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We'll see you guys there and until next time.
segments.zh: 到时候见，各位；下次再见。

segments.en: Bye everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。

segments.en: Happy Boxing.
segments.zh: 快乐的拳击。
